#1898. Paul Scholes blasts ’embarrassing’ Man Utd lap of honour after Aston Villa draw

Paul Scholes has urged Manchester United’s struggling players to ditch ’embarrassing’ laps of honour after games.

The Red Devils are sitting 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break after winning just one of their ten games so far this season.

The last time United were in such a low position at this stage of the season was in 1986, while their record of eight league games without a win has only happened once before in the club’s history.

Michael Carrick and the Manchester United squad walked around the pitch applauding the fans following a humbling 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the end of last month.

Carrick was serenaded by the United fans despite the club’s dismal position but the supportive chants soon turned to boos directed at the players once the ex-England midfielder made his way down the tunnel.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The squad performed a similar lap of appreciation after Sunday’s thrilling 4-4 draw with Aston Villa but Manchester United legend Scholes was less than impressed by the gesture.

‘I tell you one thing they need to do, stop doing these laps of honour after every game,’ Scholes said on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

‘What the f**k. It’s so bad. Jesus, it’s embarrassing. Every game’s like the last game of the season. Just get off!’

Fellow former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt added: ‘That’s pissing me off as well. A lap of honour after a draw…’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Gary Neville praised the ‘persistence’ of Carrick’s side but was also critical of the post-match scenes, claiming the players are ‘almost causing themselves emotional damage’.

‘You have got to admire their persistence, they kept going,’ Neville told NBC Sports. ‘The defensive errors were shocking and we’ll discuss that shortly.

‘But this lap around the pitch… I played for Manchester United 602 times and I always appreciated the fans at the end of the game.

‘But this pattern of them walking around the pitch after defeats by Bournemouth and a 4-4 at home against Aston Villa, it’s almost painful to watch. They’re almost causing themselves emotional damage.

‘This just can’t go on, can it? It’s absolutely desperate. Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation.’

The hierarchy at Old Trafford are currently reviewing Carrick’s position and weighing up whether to make a change during the international break.

Man Utd’s interest in the Argentine head coach dates as far back as 2016, with Pochettino even meeting Sir Alex Ferguson for dinner while in charge at Spurs.

He continued: “In any case, that lunch with Sir Alex had absolutely nothing to do with it.

He explained: “I was under contract at PSG.

“After our Champions League elimination against Real Madrid, we had no option but to make sure we secured the Ligue 1 title at least.

“United were in a hurry to announce their new manager before the end of that season because the situation had become unsustainable. I couldn’t negotiate, whereas Ajax gave Ten Hag the flexibility to do so.”

The former Southampton manager also told L’Equipe earlier this year that he would relish a chance to return to the Premier League.

#1896. Man Utd manager latest: Jason Wilcox faces 'huge' Michael Carrick decision as Carrington talks set

By Lewis Blain | 09 Nov 2026 08:16, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 20:47

Manchester United chiefs are set to hold a meeting at Carrington early next week to discuss Michael Carrick's future as first-team manager.

The Red Devils head into the international break third from bottom in the Premier League after another disappointing result against Aston Villa.

Red Devils director of football Jason Wilcox now faces a significant decision over whether to continue backing Carrick or make a change in the dugout.

United played out an entertaining but frustrating 4-4 draw with Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, having twice fought back from two-goal deficits.

Unai Emery's side raced into a 2-0 lead inside four minutes, but Carrick's team responded to level the scores before half-time. Villa then struck twice again early in the second half, only for United to produce another comeback and rescue a point with two late goals.

However, the result leaves United with just eight points from their opening ten league matches, leaving them just one point off Crystal Palace at the foot of the table, with the Eagles now planning to make a managerial change of their own.

TEAMtalk journalist Graeme Bailey reports that a meeting between United's hierarchy is scheduled for early next week, with Carrick's position firmly on the agenda.

Bailey said the meeting had already been planned before the recent fixtures, while the club had previously considered Carrick's position following the AFC Bournemouth match.

Wilcox, who has reportedly backed the current manager, is understood to be the key decision-maker and will ultimately determine whether Carrick remains in charge.

United have also conducted due diligence on potential alternatives, including Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Emery.

If United are going to make a managerial change, the timing of the international break offers a potentially useful opportunity.

With domestic football paused for a week, a new manager would have some breathing space to assess the squad, introduce initial ideas and begin preparing for the next run of fixtures without immediately being thrown into another match, with a tough trip to Anfield to face Liverpool next up.

However, changing the manager would not automatically resolve United's deeper problems. Whoever arrives would inherit the same squad deficiencies and would need significant backing to make meaningful improvements.

Emery, for example, appears an expensive and unlikely option given an imminent new deal has signalled a clear commitment to Aston Villa, while other targets would also need convincing that Old Trafford offers a stable project.

Wilcox therefore faces a 'huge decision' as Bailey explains - either continue with Carrick and hope the performances improve, or use the international break to give a replacement the chance to make an early impact.

Pochettino spent a season-and-a-half at Paris Saint-Germain in 2021-22, winning Ligue 1 and the Cope de France.

#1891. England XI vs Croatia: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Nations League

Dan Burn and James Hill have been added to the England squad as replacements for Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa ahead of Thursday’s match against Croatia.

The Three Lions face Croatia at Wembley Stadium in their penultimate Nations League group game, before completing their group-phase in Madrid against world champions Spain on Sunday.

Manchester City centre-back Guehi was assessed over the weekend after being substituted with a hip injury at half time of their defeat to Nottingham Forest but has now pulled out of the squad.

In his place, Thomas Tuchel called up the 34-year-old Newcastle defender. He had said on Friday that “difficult phone calls” had been had with Burn, Dean Henderson and Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson when leaving them behind. But the former is now in as Guehi’s replacement.

Meanwhile, it was announced on Tuesday morning that Konsa will not be available for the Croatia game, but is expected to return to full training later in the week ahead of the Spain fixture.

As such, Tuchel must decide whether to hand Hill a senior debut or reshuffle his defence with Ben White coming in at right-back, thus allowing Jarell Quansah to partner Burn in the middle.

Captain Harry Kane is expected to start and will overtake Peter Shilton to become England’s all-time most-capped player.

Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka (injury) and Noni Madueke (selection decision) are not in the squad this month but the head coach has explained that he sees his options on the right wing as being Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha, Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White and Fulham’s Josh King.

Declan Rice is back in the mix and available after missing the last international break due to load management.

Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund, brother of Real Madrid’s Jude, is in the squad for the very first time at senior level. He, King and the Brighton veteran goalkeeper Jason Steele are the only uncapped players among Tuchel’s squad.

#1890. Crewe Alexandra vs Wigan Athletic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 09 Nov 2026 09:50, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 09:53

Wigan Athletic travel to Gresty Road on Tuesday night to face Crewe Alexandra in their third and final EFL Trophy group-stage fixture.

The hosts can still secure qualification for the knockout stages but need to pick up at least a point, while the Latics head into the midweek encounter top of Northern Group B and firmly in control of their own destiny.

Having been relegated from League One at the end of the 2021-22 season, Crewe Alexandra have spent the past five campaigns in the fourth tier, where they are hoping to mount a serious promotion challenge after making a promising start to the 2026-27 season.

After falling away from the playoff race with three defeats and a draw in their final four matches last season to finish 11 points short of seventh, Crewe have made a much stronger start this time around and sit in the League Two top four after 14 matches.

Led by Lee Bell, who celebrated his fourth anniversary in charge last week, Crewe have won five, drawn seven and lost two of their opening 14 league matches to collect 22 points.

However, defeats to Exeter City and Chesterfield, along with a home draw against Barnet, have allowed leaders Salford City to open up a nine-point advantage.

Bell's side successfully carried their early-season momentum into their EFL Trophy campaign, thrashing Aston Villa Under-21s 4-1 in their opening group fixture thanks to goals from Luke Offord, Adrien Thibaut and a brace from Jack Lankester.

Despite drawing with Blackpool in normal time before losing on penalties at the start of October, the Railwaymen have collected four points from their opening two matches and need a positive result on Tuesday to reach the knockout stages for the third consecutive season.

As for Wigan Athletic, they head into their second cup fixture in the space of four days after booking their place in the second round of the FA Cup with a 3-0 victory over Boreham Wood.

Demonstrating their pedigree in the competition, which they famously won in 2013, the Latics swept aside their National League opponents to claim their first away victory of the campaign, with an early strike from Jon Mellish followed by a brace from defender Morgan Fox.

It has been a difficult start to the 2026-27 season for Gary Caldwell and his side, who currently sit in the League One relegation zone after recording three wins, two draws and nine defeats from their opening 14 matches.

Although no side in the third tier has suffered more defeats than Wigan, they travel to Cheshire on the back of their best run of form so far this season, with Saturday's FA Cup success following a victory over Bromley and a home draw against Mansfield Town.

Having collected maximum points from their opening two group matches, the Latics can still progress to the knockout stages even if they lose on Tuesday, marking a significant improvement on last season when they finished bottom of Northern Group A.

Having both secured victories in the FA Cup at the weekend, Crewe and Wigan are expected to make several changes for their return to EFL Trophy action.

Crewe have recently brought James Jones back to the club on a short-term deal until the New Year, and although he was an unused substitute in their FA Cup win over Wimbledon, he could be in contention to start on Tuesday.

Lankester has scored twice in two EFL Trophy appearances this season but has not featured since the second group fixture more than a month ago, and he is expected to remain unavailable for this encounter.

Wigan, meanwhile, will once again be without Scott Hogan, who missed Saturday's trip to Boreham Wood after being forced off during the first half of their previous match against Mansfield Town.

Dara Costelloe is also set to remain on the sidelines, with a groin injury expected to keep him out for the next four weeks.

James Carragher is expected to retain his place at the centre of a back three alongside Finley Burns and Welsh defender Fox, who will be full of confidence after scoring twice in the FA Cup victory.

Crewe Alexandra possible starting lineup:

Booth; Dancey, Offord, Graves, Ure; Moore, White; Ewusi, Thibaut, Gibson; McNeill

Walsh; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett, Weir, Power, A. Harris; Burrowes, Saydee, Mellish

With Wigan arriving in their best form of the season and boasting the advantage of playing a division above their hosts, we expect Caldwell's side to complete the group stage with a third successive victory.

Although a win would represent only their second away success of the campaign, the Latics should have enough quality to demonstrate their superiority over a side competing in the fourth tier.

#1889. Arsenal star told he should be banned for life from playing for England by Tottenham legend

Ben White’s plea to be forgiven for snubbing England has fallen on the deaf ears of Chris Waddle who believes the Arsenal star should never play for the Three Lions again.

The former Brighton defender believes England fans would not boo him if they knew the full story of his exit from England’s 2022 World Cup squad.

But the 29-year-old insists he will not ‘throw anyone under the bus’ by talking about it.

White walked out of the camp in Qatar due to ‘personal reasons’, reported to be an alleged fallout with assistant manager Steve Holland, and subsequently made himself unavailable for the rest of Sir Gareth Southgate’s time in charge.

He returned to Thomas Tuchel’s squad in March, but was jeered by England supporters before being ruled out of this summer’s World Cup through injury.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The 29-year-old says he stands by his decision of four years ago, but is looking forward to his ‘story continuing’.

‘It’s something that I’ve not spoken about, and I won’t go into detail about it,’ White told talkSPORT. ‘Yes, it’s a decision that I don’t want to be talking about anyone negatively or throwing anyone under the bus.

‘It was obviously not an ideal situation, and (a decision) that I probably still would make.

‘There’s loads of things that happened and communication wasn’t great. It’s something that I don’t want to throw anyone under the bus. I think there’s a lot of people who tried to do that to me. So it’s something that I wouldn’t want to do to someone else.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He added on BBC Radio 5 Live: ‘I don’t think I would (change decision).

‘Obviously, I was a bit younger. I’m a bit older now. I think, as a person, I’m quite real, and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make.

‘It’s one that I’m not happy about, but obviously it happened, it’s time to move on.

‘It’s such a privilege to ever get close to playing for your country, something I probably didn’t even dream of because I didn’t think it would be anywhere near my reality.

‘There’s been a few bumps, I’m obviously here now, and looking forward to this story continuing.’

The basis of White’s alleged falling out with Holland is thought to be over an interview where the Arsenal defender admitted to not watching football on television.

Select your team for football news tailored to you Close

He said: ‘To be fair, I don’t. I don’t know if I actually said I don’t like it because people say I don’t like football, which is obviously not true.

‘It’s because I don’t watch it, which I think is quite normal for someone who does a job and then doesn’t go home and then continue watching that job.

‘But I think it’s my way of release from the game because it’s so intense, obviously.’

White’s return to the fold under Tuchel was eventful as he was booed in a friendly against Uruguay, where he scored and then gave away a penalty.

‘I think before the game, I was thinking, just don’t…not stand out, but just nice and easy, you know,’ he added.

‘Then I came on and obviously get booed. Then I score. Then I give away a pen. So it was obviously full of emotions that night, and it was a good night.

‘Everyone can do whatever they want. You know, it’s fine with me. Whatever they want to do, and I think just think about maybe not knowing the full story. And if they did, maybe they wouldn’t.’

White’s candid explanation for his actions and desire to rebuild his reputation holds no water with Waddle who was capped 62 times by England.

‘Listen, Ben White shouldn’t be in the England squad, that’s my opinion,’ the former Tottenham winger told iGaming.com.

‘He refused to represent his country. I’m surprised Thomas brought him back in, and I don’t get why he has.

‘There might be a shortage of full-backs, but when somebody turns down playing for their country, like Ben White did, to me that’s a lifetime ban. I’d say, ‘Forget it mate, on my watch you’re not getting back in’.

‘He’s not playing every game at Arsenal, so he’s a surprise inclusion to me. I think the England fans will show him what they think of what he did if he plays, because you don’t turn your country down and say, ‘I’m not interested in international football.’ I There are not many many players who would ever do that, and there are even fewer who have been able to resurrect an international career after doing so.

‘Once you turn your country down, there should be an asterisk next to your name that means you will never get the opportunity to put on that England shirt again. End of story.

‘It’s all right coming out and saying, ‘Well, that was that time and this is now,’ but he knew what he was doing. If he didn’t want to play then, why does he want to play now? As I say, he’s not the permanent right-back at Arsenal.

‘Okay, he’s got that versatility where he can play centre-half as well. From Tuchel’s POV, I think it’s a very, very strange call-up for him to make and one that he probably doesn’t need to make.’

Atletico Madrid are plotting an ambitious January transfer move for out-of-favour Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi helped bring Arsenal’s painful 22-year wait for a Premier League title to an end last season, making 34 starts across the top-flight campaign while racking up five goals and an assist.

The 27-year-old was also instrumental in the Champions League as the Gunners progressed to the final for just the second time in the club’s history, only to lose on penalties to PSG in the final.

However, a combination of injury problems, Myles Lewis-Skelly’s resurgence in central midfield and the high-profile summer arrival of Bruno Guimaraes have seen Zubimendi slide down the pecking order in north London.

All seven of Zubimendi’s league appearances this season have come from the substitutes bench and the Spain international has grown frustrated with his peripheral role under Mikel Arteta, desperate for more minutes.

Zubimendi’s name is said to have ’emerged as a potential target’ and the 2026 World Cup winner could be ‘one of the prized signings’ of the January transfer window if his struggles continue at Arsenal.

Chelsea and Tottenham fans react as Pochettino is linked with shock return

In 2028, Man United will celebrate its 150th anniversary and Berrada has previously gone on record stating the plan to mark the landmark achievement is by winning both the men's and women's league titles.

In an interview with the United We Stand fanzine, he said: "It's establishing a series of targets within a timeframe so we can focus our efforts and energy on that goal.

"Can the team win the Premier League title by 2028? Of course.

"We've just finished 15th and it seems an impossible task. But why not aim for it? Why not do everything in our power?

"I firmly believe we can do it. We have two or three summer windows to build a team to start competing to win the Premier League."

Berrada, who first shared his "Project 150" vision with staff in September 2024, said he was well aware of the challenge ahead as United were coming off their worst top-flight season since relegation in 1973-74 and defeat to Tottenham in the Europa League final.

Speaking after United’s third-place finish last season, Berrada doubled down on his target.

"Ideally, we do it next season, and if not, then the following season. I think we're in a good place," he said on Inside Man Utd.

"We've seen some really good progress on the pitch this season, and we're going to continue building on that.

"We're going to continue investing in different areas of the club. There are other objectives off the pitch that we'd like to achieve as well. One of them is to be financially sustainable, to introduce commercial innovation in the club."

However, with Man United languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after 10 games of the new season, Berrarda’s confidence has been called into question.

Furthermore, Carrick - set to be sacked as Man United manager by the end of the week - stressed there was no timeframe for the club to be crowned champions of England again.

"I firmly believe we can do it. We have two or three summer windows to build a team to start competing to win the Premier League

“I think the goal, being at this football club, the goal is always to win,” he told reporters last month. “There's no timeframe on that from my perspective. It's as soon as we possibly can. And I think we understand we're still making steps to get there.

“For us to win the Premier League is a massive step, of course it is, but it's definitely something we're striving for and we've got to keep pushing for it.

“We're trying to build to get to somewhere where we haven't been for too long. I know that, and sometimes you've got to go through different ways and different pathways to get to the top.”

#1884. Liverpool: Trey Nyoni impact under Andoni Iraola cannot be ignored

By Axel Clody | 09 Nov 2026 09:57

In a transfer market that moves as many millions as the Premier League’s, where all 20 clubs are looking to invest in signings that can raise the level of their squads, the answer is often already within the club. One such case is Liverpool’s.

Trey Nyoni’s performances so far, a midfielder of just 19, show that the youngster could be the solution for the starting XI until the end of the season. With maturity above the average, the Englishman shows excellent vision, courage on the ball and quality in building play.

Against Arsenal earlier this month, in the Premier League, he led the match in accurate passes (53), pass accuracy (96%) and line-breaking passes (14), according to Opta data.

Against Fenerbahce last Wednesday, he then scored his first goal for Liverpool in a secure performance in midfield. The numbers with and without the ball also caught the eye.

Accurate passes: 89/96 (93%) Passes in the opposition half: 58/64 (91%) Passes in own half: 31/32 (97%) Long balls: 4/5 (80%) Tackles: 2/2 Interceptions: 3 Ball recoveries: 9 Ground duels: 2/4 Blocked shots: 1

In a midfield that is falling short, Nyoni is the positive news that could change Liverpool’s outlook.

That was Nyoni’s 12th game for Liverpool at the start of this season, half of them as a starter. The youngster was discovered in 2023, when he stood out for Leicester City’s Under-18s at just 15 years old.

His prominence in Liverpool’s youth system soon caught the attention of then manager Jurgen Klopp. At 16, he made his debut for Liverpool at Anfield, in an FA Cup match. Before the youngster replaced Harvey Elliott, Klopp and Nyoni looked at each other and smiled together, perhaps both already knowing the future in store for the gem.

In the last transfer window, Liverpool turned down a £30m proposal from Nottingham Forest because they believe in the talent and future of their prospect. So far, that faith looks justified.

The club and the player are in advanced talks over a new contract. The board understand that the midfielder, like winger Rio Ngumoha, is one of two gems with an enormous future who can put their names in the history of the club.

The good news for Nyoni is also that the opportunities he has received from Iraola can be seen more as a belief that he will be a starter for a long time than as a rotation strategy, merely offering a few minutes to a young reserve.

At Bournemouth, Iraola led a talented team of players under 23, with names such as Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, among others. He not only managed them, but developed the prospects, raising the talent of each one.

In a season in which Liverpool have many question marks and few answers, Nyoni looks a success. There is still plenty of room for improvement for the gem, but the future, and the present itself, are promising.

#1883. Arsenal set price for Chelsea to sign Martin Zubimendi after Real Madrid approach

Chelsea have revived their interest in Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi ahead of the January transfer window but face competition from Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid.

The Blues were one of a number of clubs to express interest in signing Zubimendi last summer but the Spanish World Cup winner ended up staying at Arsenal.

Zubimendi enjoyed a bright start to his Arsenal career following a £60m move from Real Sociedad in 2025 but became a less influential figure in Mikel Arteta’s side towards the end of last season.

The 27-year-old appeared fatigued in the second-half of the campaign and lost his place in the team, with a then 19-year-old Myles Lewis-Skelly starting the Champions League final ahead of him.

Zubimendi saw the intense competition for places at the Emirates Stadium only increase in the summer as Arsenal spent £75m to sign Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

As a result Zubimendi is still waiting for his first Premier League start of the season, with his lack of game-time sparking renewed speculation over his future in north London.

Zubimendi’s frustrating spell at Arsenal has not put off potential suitors, with Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid all ‘monitoring’ the Spaniard ahead of the January transfer window.

According to The Independent, all three clubs suspect a January deal could be possible and view Zubimendi as an ideal acquisition given he is now a Premier League, World Cup, European Championship and Nations League winner.

It is claimed Arteta still regards Zubimendi as a ‘valuable option’ given Arsenal expect to challenge for both the Premier League and Champions League yet again this term.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

But Arsenal’s desire to sign a new forward in January may depend on a major sale and Zubimendi would be an obvious candidate to be moved on, although the English champions would want to recoup at least the £60m they paid for him 16 months ago.

Xabi Alonso is keen to bolster his options in midfield after Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City on deadline day last summer and knows Zubimendi well from his time at Real Sociedad.

Jose Mourinho also intends to sign a new midfielder in January and Real Madrid have been huge admirers of Zubimendi ever since he broke through in La Liga.

But Real face competition from arch-rivals Atletico, with reports in Spain claiming Diego Simeone is ‘dreaming’ of signing Zubimendi from Arsenal.

Zubimendi came on as an injury-time substitute in Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Hull City on Saturday, a result that sent Arteta’s side six points clear at the top of the table.

#1882. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”

Possession: Arsenal 55%-45% ChelseaShots: 16-13Shots on target: 9-5Corners: 5-3Touches in opposition box: 44-25

The final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

That is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

Chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

Arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a big club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

It has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

Estevao is brought on for Chelsea in place of Neto.

Pedro wins a corner off Gabriel out on the left in front of the travelling Chelsea fans. Gusto’s delivery to the back post is caught at the second attempt by Raya.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

As it stands, Manchester City will be the only team with a 100% record after three games.

I think Chelsea are now 19 Premier League games without keeping a clean sheet, dating back to last season.

A few Chelsea players were having a moan at referee Christopher Kavanagh as they went off for half-time. But Alonso’s players need to calm down and keep their cool. There were signs the Blues’ old disciplinary problems could rear their head again with Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer being booked. Romeo Lavia also squared up to Ben White for no real reason. Chelsea have to keep 11 players on the pitch.

Possession: Arsenal 58%-42% ChelseaShots: 10-6Shots on target: 6-3Corners: 2-0Touches in opposition box: 26-13

A really enjoyable half of football, even if it was slowed down a little in the last few minutes by a series of niggly fouls. Arsenal are the better team here but Chelsea are definitely dangerous. That Neto shot off the post was evidence of how quickly they can hurt the Arsenal defence.

The first half is brought to an end and it is 1-1 going into the break at the Emirates.

Chelsea hit the post late on in the half. Chelsea counter from inside their own half and Pedro whips a ball first time down the right channel to pick out the run of Neto. The Portuguese forward drives at Gabriel inside the Arsenal box and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot. His effort comes back off the far post and Chelsea were inches away from retaking the lead.

That left side of the Arsenal defence again. Wide open for Neto to run into the space. Chelsea looking for the early ball every time.

Tensions are boiling over as Lavia and White come to blows. As Lavia shepherds the ball out of play, White threw himself to ground and wanted a free-kick. Lavia is not impressed by White’s antics and lets him know about it.

Is Palmer in some trouble? Raya catches a free-kick into his box and gets Arsenal going on the counter with a long ball forward. With Havertz getting away from him, Palmer brings him down and takes the yellow. There was another covering defender, hence why it was just a yellow.

As we approach half-time, there have been 15 shots in total from both sides in the game with nine of those being on target.

Chelsea win it just inside the Arsenal half after good defensive work from Lavia and Pedro then spots Raya off his line. The Chelsea forward therefore opts to shoot from a long way out but drags his effort wide.

White and Havertz exchange a neat one-two down Arsenal’s right, with the latter clipping the ball to the back post. Lavia, with Saka right behind him, heads away well under pressure.

That is a decent opportunity for Rogers to get his second of the game. Pedro lays it off to him on the left side of the box and Rogers tries to curl one into the far corner but it goes wide.

Tremendous game at the Emirates. Both teams attacking one another. Chelsea have a lot of space with Pedro Neto on the right and keep using that diagonal ball. Once again, though, they look suspect in defence. The Havertz equaliser could have been stopped twice, but Chelsea defence just did not react. Fofana let Havertz past and Odegaard set a bit of a screen that stopped Lacroix getting close.

Former Chelsea player scores against former Arsenal goalkeeper. Interesting reaction from the Arsenal players to that Havertz goal: most of them ran straight back to their own half. They want to get on with this game. Suggests they can sense Chelsea’s vulnerability.

Against his former club, Havertz gets the equaliser but again there will be an offside check. It appears he is onside as he receives the ball on the right. Havertz then drives across the face of the penalty area and shoots towards the near post. Martinez should make the save but can only palm it into the corner of the net. The goal stands and it is 1-1 at the Emirates.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

I think we’d be talking about Robert Sanchez if he had let that Havertz shot in at his near post. That wasn’t great from Martinez and Arsenal fans will love reminding him of it. Great game, this.

James decides to shoot from range and he strikes it really well, forcing Raya into a good save. Arsenal then counter and it ends with Odegaard having a shot blocked. Should Havertz have shot himself rather than lay it off for Odegaard?

Back come Chelsea and Pedro nearly gets on the end of a cross from Palmer.

Palmer, who has been quiet so far, receives it on the edge of the box and he is afforded too much space. He decides to shoot and looks to curl it into the far corner but Raya gets down to his right to make the save. He had to make sure he did not spill it as Pedro was lurking.

Tzolis cross from the left having been found by a great ball from Odegaard finds Havertz near the edge of the box. Fofana makes a crucial block to deny Havertz but Arsenal have the corner out on the left. Once more, Chelsea leave plenty of players up the pitch and Fofana heads away.

Odegaard works it to Saka on the right side of the box and the latter strikes towards goal, forcing Martinez into a decent save.

The goal will not stand. Konsa was offside before Calafiori scored so Chelsea remain 1-0 up.

#ARSCHE – 12' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of goal – and determined that Konsa was in an offside position in the build-up and recommended that the goal was disallowed.

The hosts equalise with a set-piece. Pedro should clear Rice’s free-kick but completely misses it. The ball comes to Gabriel, whose shot is saved by Martinez. Konsa then hits the post before a mad scramble ensues. Calafiori then forces the ball into the net. However, VAR are checking the goal...

Hato brings Saka down not far outside the Chelsea penalty area and both Odegaard and Rice are standing over it. Chelsea have just three men in the wall. Rice is going to take...

Arsenal have a corner out on the right yet Chelsea, who are the ones defending, leave four players up the pitch rather than in their own box. Is that madness or a masterstroke? The delivery from Saka goes beyond the back post, where it is then headed back across goal. Saka gets to it and then goes down but he was offside anyway.

It looked like Chelsea left four attackers upfield for that Arsenal corner. That’s one way of reducing the traffic in the six-yard box.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first five minutes of each of their three Premier League games this season. Has that ever happened before? Thanks OptaJoe:

3 - Chelsea are the first side to score in the opening five minutes of three successive Premier League games since Newcastle United in December 2024, and first ever to do so in their first three matches of a season in the competition.Blocks. pic.twitter.com/g9bum6fQkA

Fofana brings down Havertz with a rather silly challenge and Arsenal have a free-kick out on the right, with the chance to send it into the Chelsea box. Odegaard drills it low in towards the near post and picks out the run of Calafiori. The Italian’s effort is saved by Martinez’s legs and then a mad scramble for the ball ensues. It is difficult to see where the ball is and ends up going out for a goal kick. Martinez stays down and is receiving treatment to his head. It comes as a result of Gabriel’s boot flying into Martinez’s head. Should VAR be taking a look at that one? They clear it but Gabriel might count himself lucky that a review for violent conduct was not called.

Not even two minutes into the game, Chelsea take the lead and it is a man Arsenal wanted over the summer who scores against them. Rogers, on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area, watches the ball onto his foot and volleys first time into the bottom left corner. A fine finish from Rogers and Chelsea have the perfect start. How will Arsenal respond?

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

The first goal Arsenal concede this season is scored by the first player they wanted to sign in the summer.

Wow. That had echoes of Eze scoring against Tottenham last season. Just as Spurs had missed out to Arsenal for Eze, Arsenal missed out to Chelsea for Rogers. So what happens? Of course, he scores. After just two minutes. I’m also pretty sure Rogers imitated the Thierry Henry celebration next to the corner flag just to rub salt into Arsenal’s wounds.

The two bosses, who have known each other since they were children, share a warm embrace before kick-off.

We are under way at the Emirates. Both sides have 100% records coming into this one but at least one of those will fall today.

Perhaps some early mind games from Arsenal as Chelsea were left waiting in the tunnel for a little while before Arsenal eventually emerged. Eventually both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:

Arsenal: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.Substitutes: Kepa, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman.

Chelsea: Martinez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Fofana; Neto, James, Lavia, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Colwill, Gusto, Chavarriia, Barco, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck.

"It's a London derby, it's two big clubs"Mikel Arteta speaks as Arsenal host Chelsea on Super Sunday ⚔️ pic.twitter.com/S4x7Vx3dvV

"We need to play with maturity, with intelligence" 🧠Xabi Alonso speaks ahead of Chelsea's visit to Arsenal 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/Y2egodgmY5

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has confirmed that the Ecuadorian midfielder was close but Alonso says it was not worth the risk at this stage of the season. He also confirmed that Levi Colwill being on the bench today was down to fitness.

The first game of the afternoon has just concluded at the Hill Dickinson and Everton have snatched a point at the death against Manchester United, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles scoring a screamer on his Everton debut with almost the last kick of the game to make it 2-2. It is not always particularly significant when a manager says his player can be one of the best in the world. But it is probably worth taking notice when Xabi Alonso articulates his belief that Reece James can be one of the best midfielders on the planet.

For Liverpool, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Spain, Alonso was one of the finest midfielders of his generation and also played with some of the best midfielders in the world. So the Chelsea manager knows a thing or two about what it takes.

James has long been considered – when fit – one of the best right-backs in the world. But it had already been evident before the final 24 hours of the transfer window that the Chelsea player would spend a lot of time in midfield under Alonso.

Arsenal fans, did your club do enough during the transfer window? If not, what would you have liked to have seen your club get? Have your say in he comments section at the bottom of the blog.

"We have a good chemistry"João Pedro on his relationship with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers 🤝 pic.twitter.com/eIwCL9joPg

Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

"It's another tough game"Ben White on coming up against Chelsea's front three 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/gfazGGNSA8

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

Arsenal: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.Substitutes: Kepa, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman.

Chelsea: Martinez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Fofana; Neto, James, Lavia, Hato; Palmer, Joao Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Colwill, Gusto, Chavarriia, Barco, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck.

How chaotic will Arsenal allow the game to become today? Both of Chelsea’s league matches this season have been remarkably open, to the point of silliness. Arsenal do not usually allow such things to happen on their watch. They are far too sensible for that. But, having seen Brighton create so many chances at Stamford Bridge last week, Arteta may fancy his team to do some serious damage to Chelsea’s damage if the match opens up.

There’s a slight surprise in Chelsea’s line-up with Levi Colwill dropping to the bench and Josh Acheampong coming in. That could point to Alonso changing to a back four with Acheampong at right-back and Pedro Neto playing further forwards as a right winger. Chelsea only managed 25 per cent of possession against Brighton, so is this an attempt to get more of the ball? As expected, Moises Caicedo is not fit so Reece James and Romeo Lavia will need to play well.

Your Chelsea XI.#CFC | #ARSCHE pic.twitter.com/UkSmiUVgO3

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your London derby Gunners ⚡️ 🤝 Presented by @deel

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

They have just got back under way in the second half on Merseyside and Manchester United have taken the lead against Everton through Bryan Mbeumo. You can follow the action from the Hill Dickinson here.

Will Ezri Konsa come into Arsenal’s starting lineup today? It would be harsh on Cristhian Mosquera, who has been excellent so far this season, but when you pay more than £50m for a ready-made, elite-level centre-back, these are the matches you surely want him for. Mosquera had a slight injury against Aston Villa on Monday night, which may give Arteta the perfect reason to throw his new signing into the side.

Saturday:Newcastle 2 Bournemouth 2Brentford 1 Sunderland 1Brighton 1 Leeds 1Fulham 2 Crystal Palace 3Manchester City 1 Coventry 0Nottingham Forest 0 Tottenham 0Hull City 0 Aston Villa 0

Today:Everton 0 Manchester United 0 HTArsenal vs Chelsea 4.30pm

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

#1881. England vs Croatia: Nations League prediction, kick-off time, TV, live stream, team news, h2h results, odds

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

England face Croatia in the penultimate game of the Nations League group stage, which will see captain Harry Kane become the most-capped player in Three Lions’ history.

Fresh from winning the Ballon d’Or, captain Kane is set to make England history with his 126th cap to move clear of long-time record-holder Peter Shilton.

Croatia head to Wembley, with their mauling at the hands of the Three Lions’ in Rijeka last month still fresh in the memory.

Thomas Tuchel’s side put seven past their hosts without reply, as Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka bagged braces. There were further goals from Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon, and Morgan Rogers as England wiped the floor with Croatia.

England are poised to advance to the next stage of the Nations League but currently via a second-placed finish, which would set up a quarter final with a big hitter such as France or Portugal.

Victory for England at Wembley would likely set-up a last-game decider with Spain, the winner of that match topping the group.

England vs Croatia is scheduled for a 7.45pm GMT kick-off on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

TV channel: In the UK, England vs Croatia in the 2026/27 Nations League is being televised live and free to air on ITV, with coverage of the match beginning at 7pm BST on ITV1 ahead of a 7:45pm kick-off.

Live stream: Catch the game live online through the ITVX website and app, which is free with a registration.

Live blog: You can follow all the action with Standard Sport’s live blog, featuring expert insight and analysis from England correspondent Dom Smith.

There should be another landmark reached for Ballon d’Or winner Kane on Thursday, with the England skipper set to overtake Shilton as the most capped player for the Three Lions.

Injuries for Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa have led to the late call-ups of Dan Burn and James Hill, with the latter hoping to make his England debut.

Other potential debutants include Fulham's Josh King and Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham, younger brother of England star Jude.

For Croatia, ex-Tottenham Hotspur winger Ivan Perisic is suspended after his red card last time out against Spain in Split.

After last month’s chastening 7-0 loss to England, many in Croatia are writing this game off, with calls to rest legendary 41-year-old Luka Modric for the crunch clash with Czechia later in the International window.

As mentioned above, this fixture has already produced plenty of goals. Croatia have been leaky at the back throughout the Nations League campaign, conceding 14 goals in four games. A 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Spain in their last away game indicates that England should have plenty of chances to score at home.

While the Three Lions were able to keep Croatia quite away from home, their guests on Thursday night usually score at least once. It would not be a surprise to see England match Spain’s latest result against Croatia.

England and Croatia have crossed paths in three of the last four major tournaments, with the Three Lions victorious on two occasions. However, Croatia had the last laugh - beating England in the semi-finals of the World Cup to reach a maiden final.

Overall, this is a fixture England usually win - but Croatia have inflicted major upsets before, preventing England from qualifying for the 2008 Euros with wins home and away.

#1880. Rio Ferdinand names his top choice to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Rio Ferdinand says Mauricio Pochettino is the candidate who ‘jumps off the list’ to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.

Carrick, 45, looks set to be sacked following United’s disastrous start to the 2026/27 campaign.

Manchester United are 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break, just one point off bottom spot.

Old Trafford bosses are currently reviewing Carrick’s position but a change in the dugout appears to be the most likely outcome.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with Manchester United over the past couple of months.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Pochettino has also emerged as a candidate to replace Carrick and Ferdinand has put his support behind the Argentine.

Pochettino, 54, signed an extension to his contract as USA coach after last summer’s World Cup but the deal is believed to contain a release clause.

‘People are talking about Mauricio Pochettino and it looks like he’s at the front of the queue right now,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

‘We spent some time with him and his team in the summer, they’re really good guys and competent at what they do.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I look at Pochettino and one of his biggest assets is that human element of his management and building confidence with his players. That’s a big part of Manchester United at the moment because we’ve got far too many broken individuals.

‘How that gets rebuilt, is that coaching, results or somebody coming in and putting an arm around their shoulder? It’s going to be all of that.

‘I look at that group of names and think Pochettino is the one that jumps off the list as someone who has more of the things we’re looking for to save and build a group of players.

‘I think he’s got more than the others from what I’ve seen and my interactions with him over time.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘There’s not many names jumping off the page when you look at it. People will say, “what has Pochettino won?”, but you can say the same about Eddie Howe.

‘The standards have dropped massively so let’s be realistic about where we are. There’s a process to get back there. We need to stabilise and get back in the Champions League again.’

Pochettino began his managerial career at Espanyol before his prominence rose during a short but impressive spell in charge of Southampton.

He then spent five years at Tottenham, taking Spurs to the final of both the Champions League and Carabao Cup but failing to win a trophy in north London.

Pochettino had mixed stints at PSG and Chelsea before taking over as coach of the United States in September 2024.

His USA team impressed in the group stages of last summer’s World Cup, topping Group D, but suffered a humbling 4-1 defeat to Belgium in the last-16.

Manchester United’s first game after the international break is a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool on November 22.

#1879. Photo: Leak suggests Puma will go for bold design with Milan’s 2027-28 third kit

The design of AC Milan’s third kit for the 2027-28 season has been leaked, according to a report, featuring a black base and yellow details.

The 2027-28 season will be the last with Puma as Milan’s kit partner, as an agreement worth €50m per year has been reached with Adidas from 2028-29 onwards. It’s a switch that many fans have longed for, but right now, the focus is on whether Puma will end their tenure at the top or not.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The reality is that a lot of the Puma kits, especially the ones in recent years, have been praised by the Milan fans for their design. There’s certainly no bad blood between the parties and as such, Puma is working very hard to deliver a strong output for the last season.

This morning, an image of what is believed to be Milan’s third kit for the 2027-28 season surfaced, courtesy of the usually credible Footy Headlines. The base is black with grey paint splatter effects, while the details are yellow/neon-yellow.

It doesn’t really remind us of any previous kits that Milan have worn, especially since it’s a rather bold design (but it’s a third kit, after all). Compared to the current third kit, for example, the 2026-27 edition is much more muted and clean, whereas this is very lively.

Only the chest image has been leaked so far, so we will have to wait a little longer to see the full shirt. Let’s also remember that this is an early leak and that the final design will likely differ a little. Usually, the final version tends to look better.

#1878. Premier League Team of the Week: Bruno Fernandes, Dominik Szoboszlai, Liam Delap

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 10:01, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 10:03

Arsenal sit five points clear at the top of the Premier League table heading into the November international break, with the Gunners beating Hull City 1-0 on Saturday afternoon.

Manchester City's domestic problems continued with a 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest, while Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 defeat to Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Brighton & Hove Albion and Liverpool were also victorious, but the most dramatic match of the weekend came at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon, as Manchester United and Aston Villa played out a chaotic 4-4 draw.

Here, Sports Mole presents its Premier League Team of the Week for Gameweek 10 of the 2026-27 campaign, according to the data.

Tzolakis put in an excellent performance for Hull in the team's 1-0 defeat at Arsenal on Sunday; the goalkeeper made nine saves in total, and it would have been more comfortable for the Gunners had the 24-year-old not been in such impressive form.

Hume was a standout performer for Sunderland in their 1-0 win over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light; the 24-year-old won five aerial duels and made five tackles during a strong defensive performance against Xabi Alonso's side.

Vuskovic has been an exceptional signing for Brighton, and the 19-year-old was again excellent against Brentford, winning eight aerial duels and finishing with a pass success rate of 87%.

Cunha scored an excellent goal in Forest's win over Man City, while he also helped keep Erling Haaland quiet with a strong defensive performance in Saturday's late start.

Mykolenko set up Thierno Barry to score Everton's leveller against Coventry City on Friday, while he won six aerial duels and finished with a pass success rate of 84%.

Madueke was Arsenal's best performer in Saturday's 1-0 win over Hull, with the England international completing six dribbles and finishing with a pass success rate of 85%; the 24-year-old was the biggest threat for the Gunners on the afternoon.

Teddy Sheringham believes Manchester United should look to sign Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas to add more firepower to their side.

The Red Devils currently sit 18th in the Premier League table and without a win in eight matches in the competition after their dramatic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa last weekend.

And that disappointing start to the season appears set to cost Michael Carrick his job, with the latest reports suggesting the 45-year-old will be sacked over the international break.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with Manchester United over the past couple of months.

But former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino has now emerged as a serious candidate to replace Carrick before their match against Liverpool on November 22.

In particular, the former England striker believes the Red Devils could do with some more attacking firepower, name-checking young Brighton striker Kostoulas as his ideal target in the January window.

#1876. Tottenham given Dejan Kulusevski fitness update ahead of Sweden comeback

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sweden manager Graham Potter will work closely with Tottenham when it comes to managing Dejan Kulusevski’s return from injury - pledging to have “a close dialogue” with Spurs.

Potter has managed Sweden’s national side since October 2025, five months after Kulusevski’s devastating kneecap injury.

Kulusevski played for the first time in 526 days with an appearance off the bench against Coventry City last month, so Potter has finally been able to call-up the winger for the first time.

However, Potter is well aware of the ongoing need to manage Kulusevski’s fitness.

Potter is quoted by Swedish outlet Sportsbladet as saying: “We are of course in contact with Tottenham and it is logical that we work closely with them. They have worked with Dejan for so long to get him back to the level he is at now. Therefore, it is reasonable that we have a close dialogue.

“We have a pretty good idea of ​​how we can use him. But the most important thing for us is that he is here.”

Kulusevski has required two separate surgeries on his kneecap to correct an issue first sustained while playing for Spurs at the end of the 2025 season. Immediately undergoing the knife on his patella, the 26-year-old required further surgery in March 2026 after complications arose from the initial operation.

The former Juventus man has played just 42 minutes across four games as Spurs carefully manage his return.

“It was of course a difficult time,” Potter continued when discussing Kulusevski. “But when I say it was tough, it was of course nowhere near how tough it was for him himself.

“Above all, I want to pay tribute to him for how he has gotten through the dark periods because I’m pretty sure there have been those.

“Everyone knows how important he is to us, of course. We have had to try to do what we can from a distance to support him and be there.”

Sweden welcome Bosnia & Herzegovina to Stockholm on Saturday, November 14, before visiting Poland on Tuesday, November 17.

Potter’s side are top of Group B4, with three wins and a draw from their first four Nations League fixtures.

Positive results against Bosnia and Poland should result in promotion to the top tier of the Nations League for the 2028/29 edition of the tournament.
