#1874. What will happen if Man United get relegated from the Premier League?

By Ben Knapton | 09 Nov 2026 10:04

Setting unwanted record after unwanted record under the beleaguered Michael Carrick, Manchester United - one of the most revered clubs to ever grace the English game - are facing the very real threat of losing their perpetual Premier League status.

Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa may have seen the Red Devils exhibit their fabulous fightback powers once more, but it also left them celebrating just one win from their first 10 top-flight games of the season, ensuring that they would spend the November international break in the bottom three of the Premier League table.

Only one point separates 18th-placed Man United from rock-bottom Crystal Palace, 16th-placed Nottingham Forest and 17th-placed Coventry City, and the powers-that-be will reportedly hold a meeting to discuss Carrick's future during the domestic hiatus.

A change in management ultimately prevented Tottenham Hotspur from suffering an unthinkable relegation last season, but what if the worst should happen to Man United?

Here, Sports Mole takes a look at what is likely to happen if the Red Devils drop down to the Championship for the 2027-28 season.

It was only a matter of weeks ago that Man United announced record revenues of £677.6m for the 2026 fiscal year, albeit alongside a pre-tax loss of £43m, thanks to their third-placed Premier League finish in 2025-26 and a wave of cost-cutting measures.

However, Man Utd's Championship revenue is estimated to fall to around £375m to £450m, largely thanks to a sharp decline in broadcasting revenues from the loss of Premier League TV deals.

The Red Devils recently recorded £206.8m in broadcasting revenue, but that number is projected to fall to around £55m to £65m in the second tier, and there would also be no European broadcasting boost unless they shock the continent and win the 2026-27 Champions League to qualify for next year's edition.

Man United would also have to reduce ticket prices, potentially bringing their matchday revenue down from just over £150m to just over £100m, although playing 23 home matches rather than 19 - plus the potential of playoffs - would negate that specific impact marginally.

Commercial deals would also suffer a hit, due to expected performance clauses in contracts with kit suppliers and other club sponsors, so a plethora of player sales would be inevitable in order to navigate the massive economical hit as smoothly as possible.

Carrick retains the backing of a large portion of the Man United fanbase, the players are currently receiving mixed receptions, but INEOS and the Glazer family could hardly be held in less esteemed regard.

However, Man Utd fans wondering whether relegation could be the straw that breaks the owners' back are likely to be left disappointed, as the Glazers are not predicted to sell the club even if they drop down to the Championship.

As businessmen, United's owners are supposedly waiting for the perfect moment to cash in on Man Utd, when the club's value is at its highest; in an ideal world, this would be when the Red Devils have moved into their proposed new stadium and are competing in the Champions League, not when they are languishing in the second tier.

INEOS would not survive in its current state, though; sporting director Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada would almost certainly be moved on, but Ratcliffe could alternatively try to increase his stake in the club while it is at its cheapest; however, that could not happen until 2029.

Interest from the Middle East reportedly remains after Sheikh Jassim's failed takeover bid too, and attempts to wrestle control from Ratcliffe and the Glazers could ramp up as the club's value declines.

Few are expecting Carrick to still be in charge of Man United come 2027, and the current favourites to succeed the Englishman include Mauricio Pochettino, Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

Roberto De Zerbi affirmed that he would stay at Spurs even if they were relegated last season; the Italian's loyalties were not tested to that extreme, but others' very well could be.

Neither Conte nor Pochettino would be prepared to take on a second-tier project, and the same is almost certainly true of Nagelsmann, although the 39-year-old's youth makes him a slightly more realistic option for a season in the Championship.

Instead, Howe could welcome the opportunity to rebuild the Red Devils, having already guided Bournemouth up the divisions with a limited budget while also taking charge of Burnley for three Championship campaigns.

A viable alternative to Howe is ex-Red Devils assistant and youth manager Kieran McKenna - formerly linked with the United job in 2024 - as the 40-year-old is also unattached, knows the culture of the club and guided Ipswich Town to two Premier League promotions between 2021 and 2026.

Man United players would supposedly not have to worry about any wage cuts in the Championship, as their contracts do not contain specific relegation clauses allowing the Red Devils to slash their salaries.

However, with the next Euros, Copa America and Africa Cup of Nations on the horizon, a mass exodus of big names would be unavoidable, especially with the Red Devils also needing to significantly reduce their operating costs too.

Offloading young players, or those just approaching their prime, would do wonders for the club's financial picture, so Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko, Carlos Baleba and Senne Lammens could all be moved on.

Leny Yoro, Kobbie Mainoo and Patrick Dorgu would generate decent sale figures too, but it is not impossible to envisage the young trio sticking around for the rebuild project, if they are willing to accept the potential knock-on effects for Euro 2028 selection.

The club's two highest earners - Bruno Fernandes and Marcus Rashford - would also have to take major pay cuts or depart, and both could therefore be tempted by Saudi Pro League switches despite their deep connection to the Theatre of Dreams.

Fernandes is part of a large group out of contract in 2027 too - a list that also includes Harry Maguire, Tom Heaton, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw - and none should be in line for a renewal if relegation is on the cards.

Joshua Zirkzee, Matthijs de Ligt, Noussair Mazraoui, Manuel Ugarte, Diogo Dalot and Youri Tielemans should all be on the market too, but the same cannot be said for the up-and-coming Carrington prospects.

Expect Ayden Heaven, Shea Lacey, Harry Amass and Jack & Tyler Fletcher to stick around and play central roles in Man United's second-tier season, potentially alongside the returning Chido Obi and Dan Gore, as well as veteran shot-stopper Karl Darlow.

Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is little closer to being resolved.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox on Monday flew out to Monaco for the pre-planned meeting, during which Carrick’s future will be discussed.

#1870. London Stadium to host big boxing events and increase concerts as it seeks to reduce £20m taxpayer bill

Get our award-winning daily news email featuring exclusive stories, opinion and expert analysis

The London Stadium is set to host large-scale boxing matches and increase concerts as the Greater London Authority seeks to reduce the £20 million yearly bill taxpayers face from its operation.

West Ham United’s ground owners want to challenge Wembley as the capital’s premier location for events in a bid to raise much-needed revenue.

The GLA owns the London Stadium LLP and the football team plays there under an agreement running until 2115.

Taxpayers have shouldered the £19 million yearly bill for the operating loss of the stadium.

When West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season, the £4.6 million annual rent was slashed by £2.5 million under terms set out in the club’s contract, pushing this further cost onto Londoners.

Commercial revenues from the former Olympic stadium have also fallen and the GLA will incur higher stewarding costs because there are 23 home games in the Championship compared with 19 in the Premier League.

Under plans going before Newham council on Monday, the stadium authority is seeking permission to increase annual events from 10 to 24.

Boxing and Soccer Aid will be recategorised under the plans so crowds of 85,000 people can attend, up from current restrictions of 60,000.

Maximum capacity for eight events a year will rise to 85,000, while the others will stay at the current capacity of 80,000.

Consecutive nights for concerts will also increase from three to four, under the proposals.

Last summer, the stadium hosted Take That over three nights and Metallica for two in a bid to boost revenue.

But the extra income only just covered the losses incurred by West Ham’s relegation and rent reduction.

Under the stadium authority’s proposals, capacity for all sports events will increase to 62,500 to match the capacity of West Ham games.

It is hoped that staging more boxing matches at the ground will be a huge cash raiser.

An upcoming bout between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury at Cardiff’s 80,000-seater Principality Stadium in December is expected to bring in excess of £20 million.

It comes after Mayor Sadiq Khan was urged earlier this year to sell the London Stadium to West Ham.

Labour London Assembly member Bassam Mahfouz urged Lord Khan to consider selling the stadium to the football club as way to avoid losing tens of millions of pounds a year.

He said the current arrangement, where West Ham pay rent to use the stadium as their home ground, had proved “disastrous” for London taxpayers.

Over the summer, Lyn Garner, Chair of London Stadium LLP, warned that “the financial situation remains challenging”.

“In 25/26, we are going to finalise the accounts at around a £19m operating loss,” Ms Garner told a meeting of City Hall’s Economy, Culture and Skills Committee.

“This is not unusual. It's been in this ballpark for some time. We have a few peaks and troughs, depending on how many summer events we have.”

She added that 25/26 had been a “particularly bad year for London Stadium, with only two summer concerts”.

#1866. The 10 best footballers in the world: Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe ranked

By Andrew Delaney | 09 Nov 2026 10:29, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 10:29

A new king of the global game was crowned at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, with Bayern Munich's Harry Kane becoming the latest name to follow in the footsteps of football icons including Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo to claim the most prestigious individual prize of all.

Kane, 33, continues to find the back of the net at an impressive rate, netting 10 times in 15 appearances for Bayern this season, in addition to coming up with 10 assists.

Kane pipped the likes of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to become the latest first-time winner of the Ballon d'Or, but does that make the England international the current best player in the world in our eyes?

Here, Sports Mole casts its vote for the 10 greatest active footballers on the planet right now.

Few players illustrate just how much the game has changed over the past decade or so than Hakimi, whose attacking ability from right-back was a leading factor in Paris Saint-Germain finally ending their Champions League hoodoo in 2025 and then winning it again one year later.

Hakimi is the best full-back in world football and therefore had to make this list, as his form has been so important to back-to-back Champions League winners PSG.

Dembele is currently on the sidelines with a hamstring injury, but it would have been incredibly harsh to leave him out of this list given his standing in the game.

The France international has scored four goals and registered six assists in 10 appearances for PSG this term, and he will be vital to their chances of glory once again in 2026-27.

Haaland's overall performance level has been criticised in the early months of the 2026-27 campaign, but he has still come up with 14 goals in 14 appearances.

The Norway international is now on 176 goals and 30 assists in 212 appearances for Man City, with the 26-year-old simply a goal machine.

However, Man City's off-the-field issues could lead to his departure sooner rather than later.

Arsenal simply must have one representative in the top-10 list considering their form this season, and their indomitable midfield metronome gets the nod.

Perhaps the best compliment one can pay Declan Rice is that no-one is talking about his transfer fee as a waste of money, as the England international has been worth every penny of the £105m that Arsenal spent on him.

Devastating from any dead-ball situation, an unrelenting ball carrier and reliable in front of goal when the opportunity presents itself, Rice has helped elevate Arsenal to new levels.

Vitinha has played a vital role in Paris Saint-Germain winning back-to-back Champions League titles, and he is arguably the biggest midfield talent in world football.

Few can dictate a match in the way that the 26-year-old can, and his performances during the 2026-27 campaign have once again been of an incredibly high level.

#1864. Jack Grealish is EXILED by Everton: Ex-England star is still being left out, confirms boss David Moyes, after boozy nights at pubs and karaoke

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 08:52 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 19:01 EST, 5 November 2026

David Moyes has confirmed that Jack Grealish will be absent for Everton's clash with Coventry City on Friday following disciplinary action last week - and said he may not even return after the international break.

The 31-year-old was dropped for back-to-back matches against Newcastle following a 'breach of club discipline' and will not be part of the Toffees' matchday squad for the third game on the spin tomorrow night.

'No, Jack is not available,' Moyes said on Thursday. 'I wouldn't give you the plan, but we will be working with Jack again soon.'

Moyes was then questioned by reporters whether the club and Grealish will mend their relationship over the upcoming international break, which is set to span two weeks.

'We'll see,' Moyes replied. 'We need to wait and see how things go.'

Asked if Grealish is currently training Moyes added: ‘I would rather not answer your question.’

Grealish, who has made seven appearances since rejoining Everton for a second season-long loan spell in the summer, has been exiled since failing to show up for a training session on Monday last week. It is understood staff struggled to make contact with the winger.

The Manchester City loanee has since returned to training but is yet to feature for the club since the punishment, having missed both the Carabao Cup 3-1 win over Newcastle and the Premier League victory over the Magpies on Monday.

Jack Grealish remains exiled by Everton - with the winger not available for their game on Friday

Grealish has missed Everton's passed two games after being disciplined for missing training

Grealish had made four successive starts before he missed Everton's 2-0 defeat by Arsenal on October 24 due to illness.

It is thought Moyes had reservations about re-signing Grealish this summer after similar issues last season and last week the manager made it clear that he backed the 'club decision' to discipline the once England international.

Moyes said: 'You probably know I'm not going to give any details, it is a club decision and I support that decision. It is something I don't want to speak too much about.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it. All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job.'

Grealish is reported to have had back-to-back nights out prior to the Toffees' defeat in north London.

The three-time Premier League winner attended the Pride of Britain awards at the Grosvenor House hotel in London on October 19 where he presented the Child of Courage award to 12-year-old Zac Howells.

He is then reported to have finished the night of celebration off at Bam Karaoke Box, a karaoke hotspot in Victoria, central London. According to the Sun, he stayed up until the early hours of the morning singing with his friends and enjoying the drinks on offer.

Grealish is reported to have gone on consecutive nights out after attending the Pride of Britain Awards on October 19

The next day, Grealish is believed to have returned to Cheshire, where he and many of his footballer friends live, to meet team-mates Jordan Pickford and Tyler Dibling at The Mauldeth pub in Wilmslow.

The trio, joined by Grealish's former City team-mate and captain Kyle Walker, where they watched Paris Saint-Germain's thrilling Champions League victory over Barcelona. A witness claimed to the Sun that they enjoyed a few drinks.

Without Grealish once again, Everton are seeking to secure a third win in a row when they come up against former Toffees boss Frank Lampard and his Coventry team.

Their only injury concern ahead of the fixture is Jarrad Branthwaite, who Moyes admitted they have been nursing since he hobbled off late on at St. James' Park with cramp.

The Scot was speaking ahead of his 592nd game in charge of Everton, which will see him draw level with Harry Catterick’s record of the most games managed for the club.

‘I got told about it a few weeks ago,’ said Moyes, who has overseen more than 1,200 games during his coaching career. ‘I didn’t realise I’d got that close.

‘Harry Catterick’s name has always been mentioned alongside Howard [Kendall’s] name. I’m very proud to be up there, to be spoken of in terms of games. I wish I had the trophies to go with what they had.’

Victory over Coventry could see Everton move into the top-four places ahead of the November international break.

‘I think there’s lots to be positive about because of how they [the players] have been doing generally,’ said Moyes. ‘I feel we could have been doing better had we not lost some players last summer. I think it would have kept us right in and amongst it.

‘I think all you can try to do is get as many wins as you can and perform as well as we have. I think the players, in the main, have had good moments in games.’

Key to Everton’s form has been the goals of Thierno Barry. The 24-year-old has netted eight this term, already as many as he managed in his first season at the club.

Asked about the striker’s improvement, Moyes said: ‘I think the first thing is, he is settling down. We took a bit of an early gamble on buying Thierno and maybe knew he wouldn’t be right, right away. That’s been the case.

‘[Erling] Haaland should be worried that he’s just behind him now,’ he joked. ‘He has to be careful, Thierno is on his back.

‘Let’s hope he can keep scoring for us. He keeps trying to improve and I hope he can do that.’

#1862. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1861. Northampton Town vs Gillingham - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 09 Nov 2026 10:29, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 10:34

Northampton Town welcome Gillingham to Sixfields Stadium on Tuesday night for their third and final EFL Trophy group-stage fixture, with the visitors sitting second in Southern Group G and the Cobblers bottom of the standings.

Northampton have lost both of their opening matches in the competition but could still sneak into the knockout stages with a sizeable victory, provided they can improve their goal difference, while Gillingham know that a point will be enough to secure qualification after Brighton & Hove Albion Under-21s have already played and lost their final group fixture.

Northampton Town's difficult run continued at the weekend as they suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to York City in the opening round of the FA Cup, with the Cobblers falling behind after just 10 seconds.

Only a few months ago, Northampton and their weekend opponents were separated by two divisions, but the Cobblers' relegation from League One and York's promotion mean the two clubs are now competing in League Two after swapping places in the football pyramid.

Under Chris Hogg, Northampton would have been hoping to make an immediate return to the third tier this season, but their early performances suggest that could be a difficult task, with 14 points from 13 league matches leaving them just two points above the relegation zone.

Although the EFL Trophy is unlikely to be a major priority for Hogg and his side, their performances in the competition have been disappointing, particularly after reaching the knockout stages last season.

The Cobblers head into their final group fixture without a point to their name, having suffered defeats to Brighton & Hove Albion Under-21s and Cambridge United in their opening two matches.

As for Gillingham, Gareth Ainsworth's side made a reasonably encouraging start to the 2026-27 League Two campaign, recording five wins, five draws and four defeats from their opening 14 matches to sit just two points outside the automatic promotion places.

The Gills entered Saturday's FA Cup encounter as favourites against National League opposition Barrow, but they were made to work hard at Priestfield Stadium by a side who had gone 10 matches unbeaten in all competitions.

With the tie heading towards extra time, Innes Cameron struck a dramatic stoppage-time winner to secure a 1-0 victory for Gillingham and prevent Barrow from progressing to the second round.

That narrow success has done little to disguise the visitors' inconsistent recent form, however, with Ainsworth's men recording two wins, three defeats and a draw across their last six matches in all competitions.

Nevertheless, Gillingham remain in a strong position to progress from Southern Group G, knowing that a draw on Tuesday would be enough to secure their place in the knockout stages.

Northampton Town form (all competitions):

Northampton will be forced into a change between the posts after goalkeeper Zach Jeacock was forced off with an injury just 12 minutes into their heavy FA Cup defeat against York City.

James Dadge is the most likely candidate to replace him on Tuesday, while Jeacock will join Sam Hoskins in the treatment room, with the latter also unavailable due to a hamstring problem.

Gillingham, meanwhile, have the option of retaining the same starting XI that featured in their most fixture, although Ainsworth is likely to make several changes.

Rohan Luthra started the Gills' previous group match and could replace Oliver Wright in goal, while Bradley Dack is also in contention to return after not featuring since Halloween.

Ainsworth is expected to retain his familiar back three, although Omar Beckles could be rested for the trip to Northampton while former Cobblers striker Tom Eaves could come in to face his former side.

Northampton Town possible starting lineup:

Dadge; Donacien, Moore, Powell, Briggs; Evans; Dale, Fornah, Lemonheigh-Evans, O'Brien-Whitmarsh; Warhurst

Luthra; Dobbs, Smith, Daley; Freeman, McKenzie, Coleman, Brophy; Waldock, Eaves, Dack

With Gillingham in pole position to advance to the next stage of the EFL Trophy, we expect them to make no mistakes here.

We see the away side securing a narrow win that sees them end the group stage with six points from a possible nine before returning to league action next week.

#1860. Liverpool told Dominik Szoboszlai injury latest as statement released

Liverpool will be sweating over the fitness of Dominik Szoboszlai over the next week.

The midfielder suffered a knee sprain in the Reds’ 3-1 win over Crystal Palace last time out, but he has still joined up with Hungary for this week’s international break.

The No8 has had an injury-hit start to the campaign, missing five games with a hamstring problem last month.

He returned to action in the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on November 1, before starting against Palace at Selhurst Park last weekend.

It remains to be seen whether he will play for his national team over this international window, with Hungary set to face Georgia and Northern Ireland in their final two Nations League group matches.

In a statement posted to social media, the Hungarian Football Federation said that their medical staff were assessing the Liverpool star ahead of their first match against Georgia.

“Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations,” it read.

“Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible. However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute.”

Reds boss Andoni Iraola will be hoping that the tests come back with positive results, with his side set to face Manchester United at Anfield upon the Premier League’s return on November 22.

#1857. Ben White: England legend demands 'lifetime ban' for Arsenal star after squad snub

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Chris Waddle has called for a “lifetime ban” for Ben White after the Arsenal defender’s previous refusal to represent England.

White ended a self-imposed exile from the England national set-up in March 2026 when he accepted a call-up from boss Thomas Tuchel, featuring in friendlies against Japan and Uruguay.

Before that, White had not represented his country since the 2022 World Cup, quitting the tournament shortly before the end of the group stage for ‘personal reasons’.

It has been suggested that White’s refusal to play for England stemmed from a ‘barbed comment’ made by then-assistant manager Steve Holland, with former Three Lions manager Gareth Southgate reiterating that he would call-up the Arsenal defender if he was available for selection.

Waddle, capped 62 times by his country, believes that White should never have been given the chance to play for England again.

Speaking to iGaming.com, Waddle stated: “Listen, Ben White shouldn’t be in the England squad, that’s my opinion.

“He refused to represent his country. I'm surprised Thomas (Tuchel) brought him back in, and I don't get why he has. There might be a shortage of fullbacks, but when somebody turns down playing for their country, like Ben White did at Euro 2024, to me that's a lifetime ban.

“I'd say, ‘Forget it mate, on my watch you're not getting back in.’”

The former Tottenham midfielder said he would go one step further, permanently marking White’s England record after his refusal to accept a call-up.

Waddle added: “Once you turn your country down, there should be an asterisk next to your name that means you will never get the opportunity to put on that England shirt again. End of story.”

White has been included in the Three Lions’ squad to face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League, prompting discourse about his refusal to play for England under Gareth Southgate.

#1856. Liverpool receive new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update as Hungary issue social media statement

By Ben Knapton | 09 Nov 2026 11:05

Liverpool have received a new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update from the Hungarian FA, who have announced that the midfielder is undergoing further tests on Monday.

Szoboszlai completed 69 minutes of Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace in Sunday's Premier League fixture, setting up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal before being withdrawn for Trey Nyoni.

Reds head coach Andoni Iraola revealed after the game that Szoboszlai was not feeling 100%, though, as the Hungary international appeared to be struggling with a knee problem at Selhurst Park.

Szoboszlai has nevertheless joined up with his national team for the time being, as the Magyars prepare to face Georgia and Northern Ireland in a pair of Nations League fixtures this month.

However, the Hungarian FA revealed on X on Monday morning that the Liverpool lynchpin is being examined by medical staff, although it remains to be seen whether he will pull out of the ranks.

"@_SZD10, who was substituted in the 69th minute of Liverpool FC’s match yesterday, is undergoing tests today, Monday, following the usual protocol in such cases," the Hungarian FA wrote. "We will, of course, keep the public informed of developments as soon as possible!"

Hungary sit second in League B Group 2 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, a standing which would see them qualify for the promotion playoffs taking place next March.

The Magyars are just one point below leaders Northern Ireland, though, and clinching top spot would see Hungary promoted to League A for the next cycle.

Szoboszlai started each of Hungary's four Nations League games in the September/October international break, captaining his country to successive victories over Georgia and Ukraine in their most recent two fixtures.

However, the 26-year-old then returned to Liverpool with a hamstring problem, ruling him out of the 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City, although he was fit enough to make his comeback against Brentford the following week.

Szoboszlai exacerbated his injury at the Gtech Community Stadium, though, and subsequently missed fixtures with LASK Linz, Villarreal, Chelsea and Brighton & Hove Albion, but Liverpool won all four games in his absence.

Szoboszlai made it through the entirety of the 2025-26 season without suffering a single injury - playing 53 games in total - and he only missed two matches in 2024-25 due to illness.

The 26-year-old did suffer a pair of hamstring injuries in 2023-24, ruling him out of 10 Liverpool matches in total, while his most serious injury occurred during his time with RB Leipzig.

Szoboszlai joined the German giants while recovering from a serious adductor problem, meaning he did not make his debut until eight months after joining in August 2021, having arrived in December 2020.

The midfielder has since amassed 31 goals and 27 assists in 158 matches for Liverpool, whose first game back after the hiatus comes at home to bitter rivals Manchester United on November 22.

#1855. Ruben Amorim rips into his AC Milan players after embarrassing Europa League defeat: Ex-Man United boss hits out at team's attitude and criticises 'awful' performance

Published: 16:34 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 5 November 2026

Ruben Amorim savaged his AC Milan side for their 'awful' attitude and performance in losing to Hungarian minnows Ferencvaros.

The former Man United boss presided over a 2-0 defeat in the Europa League on Thursday night in front of furious home supporters at the San Siro.

To make matters worse, the visitors even played the last 15 minutes with ten men but Milan were still unable to break through.

Amorim, 41, who was sacked from his post at Old Trafford last season and took over the Italian club in the summer, gave a brutal assessment of his team after the loss.

'When you play for Milan, you have a responsibility; you can't go out there like this,' he said at his post-match press conference.

'We're not ready to compete on both fronts in Serie A and Europe; we need to work on our approach to matches.

Ruben Amorim could hardly believe what he was seeing on a dreadful night for AC Milan

The home side suffered an embarrassing defeat by Ferencvaros at the San Siro

'There's nothing I can say tonight; we had to win; it was an important match. I can't say anything to defend the team; we need to understand what happened.'

He went on: 'Maybe I did something wrong in the last few days. Last year, the team had similar problems, and today we weren't ready; we didn't have the attitude to try to come back at all costs when we were behind.

'Tonight, we have no excuses. Whoever was on the pitch could have won this match. We have to resolve these ups and downs; we should have done many things much better, even just on second balls: that alone would have made things go differently.

'The first half, in particular, was awful; it's about ambition, attitude, and concentration. We weren't ready to move from the derby to another competition.'

Amorim's side are fifth in Serie A, seven points off top spot, and struggling massively in Europe down in 28th place – outside of the qualification spots for the knockout stages.

Even though Amorim made changes to the side that beat Inter in the derby at the weekend, he insisted the team should have had enough to beat Ferencvaros.

He went on: 'We're not mentally ready. The technical aspect has nothing to do with it. The rotation has nothing to do with it. You can't tell me that the starting line-up wasn't up to the task of winning the game.

'We gave ourselves all the chances we had, especially at the start. I take full responsibility for this, because the team is my responsibility, but we can't afford to do something like this, especially in the first half, in front of our fans, at our home. We can't do this; we have to improve, otherwise it's over.

'We want to do well in the Europa League too, we need to rotate and win like that too. We're not ready to play every three days now, but I certainly won't give up on the Europa League. We'll fight until it's over. It's a promise.'

Ferencvaros fans in the away end enjoyed one of the most memorable nights in their history

Amorim's results at AC Milan have been mixed after a positive start at his new club. He opted to take charge of the Italian giants having been out of work since his dismissal at United.

The Portuguese's reign at Old Trafford was disastrous. He oversaw the club's lowest Premier League finish (15th) after joining in November 2024.

And he only managed to win 38 per cent of United's games, taking 58 points from 47 games in the Premier League in total.

Amorim will hope the Ferencvaros result is a blip and AC Milan will have the chance to bounce back against Genoa on Sunday.

Manchester United could well be moving towards appointing a new manager.

The Red Devils look set to part company with under-fire head coach Michael Carrick this week, according to widespread reports, with a crisis meeting set to be held in Monaco on Wednesday with club executives including Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox.

Carrick’s position has come under severe scrutiny after just one win in 11 games in all competitions, and United were almost embarrassed at home against Aston Villa at the weekend, falling behind by two goals twice inside the opening minutes of either half.

It was a game that they roared back to draw, with Patrick Dorgu notching an injury-time equaliser, but the level of the overall performance was again cause for concern, with the 20-time Premier League champions mired in the relegation zone after 10 matches.

A three-strong shortlist looks to have come to the fore in terms of replacements for Carrick, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe, ex-Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann, and Mauricio Pochettino, currently the head coach of the USA national team, all considered.

Pochettino, formerly of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, has been linked with the Old Trafford hotseat before, and has emerged as a wildcard candidate after not featuring in early reporting of potential managerial targets.

Now, however, in an update given by David Ornstein on The Athletic FC podcast, it appears that the Argentine could well be United’s preferred option, should they be willing to meet the $10million release clause that the former defender has in his USMNT contract.

“Julian Nagelsmann is a name that has been mentioned, but I don’t hear that he’s one Manchester United are looking to pursue,” Ornstein said on Tuesday.

“Eddie Howe has been heavily rumoured, but I don’t hear that he’s one they’re looking to pursue. So, by the process of elimination, you get to someone like Mauricio Pochettino."

Pochettino, now 54, has been previously considered by Ineos for a couple of positions, firstly at Nice, and more recently with United.

“In 2024, When [Erik] ten Hag’s job was on the line, United spoke to Pochettino,” Ornstein continued.

“Every time we sign a contract, it’s to go to the last day of the contract,” Pochettino said in August. “If we sign a four-year contract, we need to think to arrive there. And we signed the contract because we really believe that we are going to be four years there. Because if not, it’s bad.

“If we don’t believe in that process, if we don’t believe in that journey, why (would) we sign four years? Only to be sure that we are going to receive a salary on the end of the month? That is not nice. It’s not the way that we think.

“We really signed that contract because we really believe that we can arrive to the end.”

#1851. Oxford United vs Cheltenham Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 09 Nov 2026 11:17, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 20:14

Oxford United welcome Cheltenham Town to the Kassam Stadium on Tuesday night for their second EFL Trophy group match of the campaign, while the visitors will be playing their third and final fixture in the group.

Both sides head into the contest on the back of FA Cup first-round fixtures, with the U's suffering a 1-0 defeat to Stevenage on Saturday afternoon, while the Robins booked their place in the next round with a 2-0 home victory over Halifax Town.

After spending two seasons in the Championship, Oxford United were relegated last May and entered the 2026-27 campaign among the favourites for promotion as they looked to secure an immediate return to the second tier.

Aaron Ramsey's side have made a positive impression back in League One so far, winning seven, drawing five and losing just once in their opening 13 matches to climb into third place.

Oxford also have a game in hand on the top two and could move level on points with league leaders Huddersfield Town by winning their rearranged fixture, although the Terriers' superior goal difference would likely keep them at the summit.

Given their impressive league form, it is perhaps surprising that Ramsey's side head into Tuesday's encounter having lost all three of their cup matches this season, following an EFL Cup defeat to Leyton Orient, a penalty shootout loss to Exeter City in this competition and, most recently, their FA Cup exit at the hands of Stevenage on Saturday.

However, the Welshman, who made 86 appearances for his country, fielded a much-changed side against the Boro at the weekend, underlining that securing promotion back to the Championship remains his main priority.

As for Cheltenham Town, they have entered the 2026-27 campaign as a League Two side for the third consecutive season and are aiming to mount a serious promotion challenge after dropping out of the third tier in 2024.

Former Bristol City manager Steve Cotterill arrived last season and guided the Robins to an 18th-placed finish, but his first full campaign in charge has started on a much more positive note.

Although Cheltenham have lost three of their last six matches, they currently sit fifth in the table after collecting 21 points from 14 games, even if their recent results have allowed leaders Salford to establish a substantial advantage at the summit.

Unlike their upcoming opponents, the Robins have enjoyed success in the cup competitions so far, winning both of their EFL Trophy group matches on penalties before progressing to the next round of the FA Cup on Saturday.

Goals from Jake Evans and George Miller helped Cotterill's side secure a 2-0 victory over National League outfit Halifax Town, ensuring they avoided a potential cup upset.

Having made wholesale changes at the weekend and rested several first-team regulars, Ramsey is likely to rotate his squad again and could name a side similar to the one that started Saturday's FA Cup defeat.

Simon Eastwood has featured in both matches since Jamie Cumming was sent off during a league fixture and could retain his place in goal on Tuesday night.

Captain Cameron Brannagan is expected to be rested once again, with Tyler Goodrham and Harrison Bradney among the most likely candidates to feature in midfield.

Cheltenham are also expected to make wholesale changes, particularly after Cotterill told Robins supporters "to stay home".

Joe Day was forced off after just 19 minutes of their most recent EFL Trophy fixture but has since returned to the substitutes' bench and could be restored to the starting lineup for this contest.

Former Aston Villa forward Andreas Weimann is expected to sit this one out, leaving George Miller to lead the line.

Eastwood; Long, Lacey, Golding, Leigh; Missanga, Bradney, Goodrham, Snowden; Lynch, O'Donkor

Cheltenham Town possible starting lineup:

Day; Tomkinson, Wilson, Sweeney, Nurse; Stevenson; Bickerstaff, McWilliams, McCann, Otchere; Miller

With both sides enjoying positive campaigns near the top of their respective divisions, we expect a closely fought encounter, despite the gap between them in the football league pyramid.

However, Oxford should have enough quality to claim their first cup victory of the season, and we are backing the League One side to edge a narrow 2-1 win.

#1849. Nations League permutations: What do England need to qualify for quarter-finals?

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 11:37, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 11:39

Eight teams will secure their spot in the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, with the group stage of the competition set to conclude this month.

Two sides have already booked their spot in the final eight - Spain and Portugal - and they will soon be joined by six more, with the quarter-finals set to take place in March 2026.

England are currently second in Group A3 behind Spain, with the Three Lions on the brink of securing their position in the final eight of the tournament.

The top two in each of the four groups will qualify for the quarter-finals.

Here, Sports Mole runs through the various permutations for the four groups.

France currently sit at the top of Group A1, with the Blues picking up 10 points from their four matches courtesy of a record of three wins and one draw.

Italy, meanwhile, are second on seven points, with their record in this group standing at two wins, one draw and one defeat.

Belgium are third in the section on six points courtesy of a record of two wins and two defeats, while Turkey are bottom, losing all four of their games thus far.

France host Italy on November 12, and a victory would see them qualify automatically ahead of their final game against Turkey. However, a draw with Italy would leave them on 11 points, with a win then required against Turkey to make sure of qualification.

A loss to Italy would mean that France need to beat Turkey to make sure of a spot in the final eight; two defeats, though, could see Zinedine Zidane's side finish third.

Italy would qualify if they manage to beat both France and Belgium, while beating France and then drawing with Belgium would also put them in a strong position.

A draw with France and then overcoming Belgium could also potentially be enough, but if Italy lose to France, they would need to beat Belgium and hope for favourable results elsewhere.

Italy cannot afford to lose both matches if they are to finish in the top two.

Belgium, meanwhile, would qualify if they beat both Turkey and Italy; a win over Turkey and a draw with Italy could also be enough depending on results elsewhere.

Should Belgium draw with Turkey, they would still be alive but would need other results to go their way, but a loss in either match makes it incredibly difficult for them to finish in the top two.

Turkey, meanwhile, are bottom of the section and cannot reach the top two.

Group A2 is incredibly close, with Netherlands at the top of the section on eight points, level with second-placed Greece heading into the final two matches.

Germany, meanwhile, are third in the section on five points, with Serbia fourth on zero points.

A win for Netherlands against Greece on November 13 would see them reach 11 points and leave them in a very strong position to secure a spot in the quarter-finals.

A draw with Greece then a positive result against Germany could also secure qualification for the quarter-finals, but a defeat to Greece would leave them needing a positive result against Germany and also results elsewhere to go in their favour.

Wins for Netherlands against both Greece and Germany would make sure of a position in the final eight, so that will be the goal for Xavi's side.

Greece, meanwhile, would be on 11 points with a win over Netherlands, which would leave them in a very strong position in the group ahead of the final round of matches.

A draw with Netherlands would leave them on nine points ahead of their final game with Serbia, where a win would book a spot in the final eight.

However, a loss to Netherlands would leave Greece needing to beat Serbia and then hope that Germany cannot overtake them; wins over both Netherlands and Serbia would see Greece secure a position in the quarter-finals of the tournament.

As for Germany, the national team must beat Serbia to keep their qualification hopes alive, but they would also then need to secure a positive result against Netherlands.

Anything less than four points from their final two matches makes qualification incredibly unlikely, but wins in both would take them onto 11 points, which could be enough to make the top two.

Serbia, though, are bottom of the section on zero points and cannot qualify.

Spain are top of Group A3, winning each of their four matches to collect 12 points, while England are second in the section, gathering nine points from their four games.

Croatia are third on three points, while Czech Republic are at the bottom on zero points.

Spain are already through to the quarter-finals of the tournament, and a win over Czech Republic on November 12 would secure first spot in the section.

England, meanwhile, are almost certainly in the quarter-finals; Croatia need to beat them 8-0 on November 12 to stand a chance of jumping above them in the section on the head-to-head record.

Mathematically, at this stage, England need a point to qualify, but sitting six points ahead of third-placed Croatia, it is incredibly difficult to imagine them not being present in the final eight.

Croatia lost 7-0 to England on October 3 and need to win 8-0 in their next match to have a realistic chance of progressing, with a victory over Czech Republic also required, in addition to a favour from Spain against England in the final fixture.

Czech Republic, though, are bottom of the section on six points and cannot qualify.

Portugal are already through to the knockout round of the tournament, picking up 12 points from their four matches, while Denmark are second, claiming six points from four matches.

Wales sit third in Group A4 on three points, while Norway are fourth on three points, so it is all to play for in the final two matchdays of the tournament.

Portugal can, in theory, still finish second in the section behind Denmark, but avoiding defeat against the Danes would secure first spot in the group.

Denmark need four points from their final two matches in the group against Portugal and Norway to be sure of a spot in the quarter-finals, but three points may also be enough depending on potential head-to-head tie-breakers.

Wales' route into the final eight is difficult given that they have lost both games against Denmark, who therefore have the advantage in any head-to-head tiebreaker.

The Dragons must beat both Norway and Portugal to stand a chance of finishing in the top two, but they are also relying on results elsewhere.

Norway also need to beat both Wales and Denmark, which would give them nine points, while a victory over Denmark would be important, as they would lead the head-to-head tie-breaker.

Two wins from their final two games would put them in a position to qualify, and they have a clearer route than Wales through that avenue despite currently sitting fourth.

Rio Ngumoha wears a cheeky smile as he sits in his England puffer jacket at Hotspur Way and discusses his upbringing, his hopes and dreams, and the lasting legacy of a fellow teenager.

Ngumoha, 18, is just a year younger than the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal and argues: “What he is doing [has] changed football for young players.

“Seeing what he can do so young inspires me and all the other young players in how we can just play freely. The way he plays, it’s like it’s his pitch. It’s a good challenge.”

He has been rewarded for fine form at Liverpool with another England call-up this month, and the absence of Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke gives Ngumoha a good chance of earning plenty of game time on the right wing against Croatia and Yamal’s Spain.

Tuchel has a glint in his eye whenever he speaks about Ngumoha and from the sidelines when the teen is readying himself to come on, you can tell they share a bond.

“He knows I’m quite talented, which is good,” he says. “Every time I come on he lets me be expressive, be free. I have the belief from him.”

Playing under Tuchel for England and Andoni Iraola for Liverpool are “similar” but their “language is a bit different”, he says, explaining that at England “it is a lot more structured, because you know the manager doesn't have enough time to get his ideas across — so that's why we have a lot more meetings, which is understandable.

“It was definitely difficult at the start when he [Iraola] came in [at Liverpool], but we had to adapt quickly.”

Ngumoha says he has played “a couple of times” against English football’s other talked-about wonderkid, Arsenal’s Max Dowman, but believes he has “played more with him than against him. Max is a top, top, top talent, a top player, and he'll definitely go on to reach many heights. We text each other if [one of us] scores.”

Describing his own playing style as “fearless” is not brash but simply the truth of the matter, and it is this confidence in his ability to go past players that led Tuchel to bring him along for the summer’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, handing him his debut, before a call-up for the last international break and another this month.

It was in Florida that he struck up a friendship with Fulham’s Josh King, the pair of them reunited with England this month.

Palmer has issued Pochettino verdict amid £90m Man Utd transfer theory

England legend demands 'lifetime ban' for Arsenal star after squad snub

When Arsenal youngsters will play for England after double selection boost

“Neymar, Eden Hazard, Mo Salah.” These are the names Ngumoha reels off when asked who he looked up to as a kid, adding: “Raheem Sterling pulled me to the side a couple of times and told me he could see I had talent but should never zone out in the game and should always be in the game.”

Raheem Sterling pulled me to the side a couple of times and told me he could see I had talent but should never zone out in the game and should always be in the game

Ngumoha grew up in Manor Park, a “tough area, Newham especially” but recalls playing football in “Wanstead flats, Mabley Green, Power League, Beckton, all of these places”.

He remembers his brother James, now his agent, pushing him to train after school even when he didn’t want to, and “sometimes going from school to get the train [to Chelsea academy training] was a bit tough, especially coming back late around like 11pm for a school kid, it isn't easy, but that's a sacrifice you've got to make sometimes to reach the top”.

A Chelsea academy star, they were loath to see him pinched by Liverpool in the summer of 2024.

“I needed a new challenge,” Ngumoha explains now. “I feel like if I stayed at Chelsea... not saying I wouldn't have got to the first team as quickly, because I believe in my ability, but I feel Liverpool just gave me a new pathway.

“The plan they set for me was straightforward. For me, it was a no-brainer going to Liverpool.”

Three months after his move to Liverpool, Ngumoha’s mother, Liz, left her job at a school in London and relocated to Liverpool where she “does everything for me and my brother. She’s just amazing. I can’t thank her enough.”
